label: Text
name: Tripitaka Koreana
summary:
The most complete and accurate extant version of the Chinese Buddhist canon (Tripitaka), carved onto 81,258 woodblock printing plates during the Goryeo dynasty (1237–1248 CE). The original first edition (c. 1011–1087 CE) was destroyed by Mongol invaders in 1232. In an extraordinary act of devotion and national prayer for protection from the Mongols, the Korean court commissioned a second, even more meticulous edition — each block carved from birch wood uniformly treated with sea water, dried, and lacquered, measuring 70 × 24 cm.

The resulting text has remarkably few errors over its approximately 52 million characters covering 1,496 titles in 6,568 volumes. Housed at Haeinsa Temple, the woodblocks are inscribed as a UNESCO Memory of the World (2007). They remain the textual authority for East Asian Buddhist studies.
